<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx`  _(via buildMcpBridge (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **37** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 13e0305c3391db13c75b39762f4cdd8ec8f4a28f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8c27b9038262817dd09ec47b3d6c9c68f6bca452` — the merge of head `2ba60e904c6efa353c0d4ffb34eeea82a25ae6d3` into base `13e0305c3391db13c75b39762f4cdd8ec8f4a28f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8c27b9038262817dd09ec47b3d6c9c68f6bca452 && git checkout 8c27b9038262817dd09ec47b3d6c9c68f6bca452
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 13e0305c3391db13c75b39762f4cdd8ec8f4a28f 2ba60e904c6efa353c0d4ffb34eeea82a25ae6d3 && git checkout -B drift-repro 13e0305c3391db13c75b39762f4cdd8ec8f4a28f && git merge --no-ff 2ba60e904c6efa353c0d4ffb34eeea82a25ae6d3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 13e0305c3391db13c75b39762f4cdd8ec8f4a28f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 13e0305c3391db13c75b39762f4cdd8ec8f4a28f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## L1: ACCEPT · 2026-11-17T16:45Z

Head-sha: 2ba60e904c6efa353c0d4ffb34eeea82a25ae6d3
Reviewer: seat 3 L1-c, for card #34872 (child of epic #34659; claim 6951869284; os-dev report 6953902671), at o3-G's request.

### 席位核对

**PR shape.** `Fixes #34872`, base `main`. Five paths:
- `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts` and `packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts`;
- one new test file beside each;
- one changeset.

**Declaration.** `Clause-②: no` / `Metadata-protocol: none`, and they agree. The answer's shape is unchanged; only the values of `label`, `description` and option `label` move. `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/mcp` at `patch` are right. The seat ruled no L2 (16:23Z), and I see no contract face that would change that.

**Governed / size.** `check-governed-merges --pr 34922`: NOT governed, 618 lines.

**Check-runs at 2ba60e90.** 57 runs, every one `success` or `skipped`: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` and all 10 shards, `Live E2E UI`, `Check Changeset`, `PR-body guards`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`.

**One routine, not two.**
- HTTP: `inCallerLocale` runs the `/meta` door's `translateMetaList` with the new `metaTranslationSources(deps, context, getProtocol)`. That resolves the i18n service (a throw means none), the protocol, and `metaRequestLocale`, which reads `Accept-Language`, then `?locale=`, then the i18n default.
- `datasetToolMembers` now uses the same sources. The dataset path's `envId` was `context.environmentId` before, so nothing changes there.
- stdio: `inServedLocale` runs the same routine through `defaultLocaleSources`, with `metaRequestLocale(undefined, i18n)`, which means the i18n default. That is the locale stdio `list_datasets` already used (#34833). The dataset path is folded onto the same helper with no change in behaviour.
- So one caller gets one locale for both the object and the dataset tools, on each transport.

**After the mask.** Both doors translate the object as the caller is served it: `servedToCaller` on HTTP, and `callerObjectView` on stdio. The translator rewrites the text of the fields it is given and adds none, so a masked field and its translated text both stay absent. Each new test file pins that case, and the report's two ablations (translate the declared object) leak the masked field. `declared` is still read only for the `readonly` verdict.

**What the translation does not touch.**
- `validate_expression` reads `describeObject`'s field `name` and `type` only (`mcp-http-tools.ts` around line 2806). Names never change, so its scope is unchanged.
- `optionFieldsOf` and `servedObjectDefinitionOf` still read the untranslated served object, on both doors, so the publish-gate passes judge the authored definition.
- Option `value`s are unchanged, so the ask skill's "filter an option field by its `value`" still holds.

**Tests.** 5 HTTP cases and 5 stdio cases cover:
- zh-CN for describe and list;
- the masked field;
- no preference, or `en` with no entry;
- a locale the bundle does not carry;
- no i18n service, or a resolver that throws (authored text, never an error).

The report also has a live zh-CN reading on app-crm that matches REST `/meta`.

**Docs made false?** None. Neither `connect-mcp.mdx` nor the MCP README says what language `list_objects` or `describe_object` labels come in. The changeset states the change.

### Must-fix
None.

### Should-fix
None.

### Notes
- N1. An HTTP caller that sends no `Accept-Language` now gets the i18n default locale's bundle entries. The changeset names app-crm's `amount` as "Deal Value" instead of the authored label. That matches `/meta` and is right. Anyone comparing replies across this change, such as the ask rounds under #34687, should know that a label can move with no locale sent. The scenario runner's citation check keys on object names (`citationLabels`), not labels, so its grading is unaffected.
- N2. The `list_objects` page is translated in one call per request, the same cost as `GET /meta/object`. Not owed.
- N3. The PR overlaps o3-E's #34881 and #34904 only by package, not by file (`skill-md.ts`, `mcp-server-runtime.ts` and service-analytics against `runtime/domains/mcp.ts` and `stdio-data-bridge.ts`). o3-G re-runs `overlap-check` before landing, as planned. #34928 touches neither file.

Next: o3-G lands. No seat L2 is owed. A later push owes an L1-c delta read.
